findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. With user_count=50 and limit=50 this yields 2 pages, but only one page exists. showingLast (currentPage == totalPages) is then false on the real last page, so the Next button stays enabled and paging forward shows an empty page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) instead.

findings.title: next() moves offset to user_count, producing an empty page on partial last pages
findings.body: offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count). With user_count=120 and limit=50, paging from offset 50 goes to 100, then next sets offset to min(150,120)=120. The request returns no members because offset equals the total, so the user lands on an empty page. The offset should be clamped to the start of the last page, e.g. the last page's offset is (totalPages-1)*limit, not user_count. group.js line 23 has the same clamp (offset capped at user_count), so the server-side empty result is reached through both paths.

findings.title: members endpoint accepts unbounded limit and negative limit/offset
findings.body: limit is taken straight from params with no upper bound, so a request with limit=10000000 returns every member of a large group in one response (the old code applied a limit only to automatic groups, and it was 200). A negative limit or offset is also passed to .limit/.offset, which can raise a database error (500) or behave unexpectedly. Clamp limit to a sane maximum (e.g. 1..100) and clamp offset to >= 0.

findings.title: findMembers clamps offset to user_count instead of the last page start
findings.body: offset = min(user_count, max(offset, 0)) allows an offset equal to user_count, which yields an empty page for any caller that stores an offset at the end of the list (for example after removeMember, which reloads with the current offset). After removing the last member on the final page the list shows nothing, even though earlier members exist. The offset should be clamped to a page-aligned start.

findings.title: Stale CSS selector targets the old input id group-users
findings.body: The group member input was renamed to id="user-selector" in group.hbs, but the rule `input#group-users { width: 600px; }` still targets the old id, so it no longer applies and the intended width is lost.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses PUT instead of the DELETE route
findings.body: The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route for remove_member is DELETE. The spec does not exercise the real verb and could pass even if routing changed. It should use :delete to match the route.

findings.title: Specs for the new members endpoints and paging are missing
findings.body: The PR removes the incremental add/remove specs and the update membership specs, but adds no coverage for the public GroupsController#members pagination (meta total/limit/offset, limit cap, offset past end). The new paging behaviour that the frontend depends on is untested, and the automatic-group specs depend on fixture id 1 existing.
